question: Does MAX_TRAVERSAL_BINS=50 silently drop profitable Trader Joe LB arbs?

source.method: per-swap bins crossed = abs(active bin id - previous swap's active id); LB active id only moves via swaps, so consecutive-swap id deltas equal that swap's traversal depth

tail_characterization.comment: the 86 swaps that exceed 50 bins are micro-notional dust on thin/exotic pairs
tail_characterization.dominant_outlier: USDV (max 6935 bins, max ~$1.61 notional) — a low-liquidity stablecoin whose bins are nearly empty

safety.kernel_behavior_at_cap: loop breaks at MAX_TRAVERSAL_BINS and returns LBSwapResult with remaining_in = unfilled amount (NO fabricated full fill / NO over-quote)
safety.caller_behavior: a capped swap has remaining_in > 0 and is treated as None/reject (fail-closed) — proven by crates/engine-amm/tests/trader_joe_lb_traversal_cap.rs
safety.failure_mode: false_negative_only (miss a micro-arb); never false_positive over-quote (no capital at risk)

rationale: 50 bins covers 99.985% of all LB swaps (p99.9 = 2 bins). The 0.0145% tail is micro-notional (<= $932, mostly << $60) on thin/exotic pairs — economically immaterial as atomic arbs. Raising the cap would add snapshot RPC cost (the same constant sets the +/-50 bin snapshot window in engine-rpc/lb_snapshot.rs) to chase a negligible tail, while the cap can only ever false-negative. Keep 50; document the bound; keep fail-closed.

production_constant.name: MAX_TRAVERSAL_BINS
production_constant.couples: kernel traversal cap AND the +/-MAX_TRAVERSAL_BINS snapshot window in crates/engine-rpc/src/lb_snapshot.rs
